newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower on weak Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower on weak Wall Street.

text.p: Swiss shares closed in negative territory, but above the day's lows in derivatives-driven trading.
"At the moment we are moving on a one-to-one scale to the Dow Jones," one trader noted, adding that the Swiss bourse was following the ups and downs of early Wall Street.
Electrical engineering group ABB continued to slide following Thursday's 1996 results. UBS was actively sought after a large buy order, one dealer said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended 32.1 points lower, or 0.71 percent, to 4,487.6.
The all-share SPI fell 18.16 points to 2,851.97.
Financials were generally underpinned by the favourable interest rate outlook and soaring futures on government bonds, one trader said.

UBS led the actives list, advancing 18 francs to 1,326. CS Group and SBC also firmed. Insurers Winterthur and Baloise, which had posted solid advances on Thursday, lost more than one percent. Winterthur fell 11 francs to 897.
Novartis registered shares were down 14 francs to 1,686 while Roche slumped 185 francs to 12,415.
Share rights on Ciba Specialty Chemicals closed 1.85 francs lower at 93.35.
Ems Chemie, which said 1996 group net rose 12.2 percent to 229.1 million francs, ended 15 francs higher at 5,755.
Stocks of watchmaker SMH continued to slide. SMH registereds slumped 4.25 francs to 194.25.
Elektrowatt was up three francs to 531 after a recent string of losses.
